## Prior root findings and focused reproductions

There are **no blocking correction requests** from this review. The following closes the three provisional visual findings on this candidate; it does not erase the failed earlier artifacts.

**P1-VIS-1 — corrected.** In 1B, `final-headland-reachable-stock.png` shows mostly buried material and `final-west-glass-empty-anchor.png` leaves little visible host. Those failures would force players to hunt for an invisible prompt. In current 1C media, all twelve full/empty views show plates/faceted nodules or the persistent frame/ridges. The headland and west-glass before-selection images identify the resource independently of the cue. `src/render/{environment,expedition}.ts` changes the physical-looking forms; it does not move source simulation datums or invent an LOS exemption. My geometry rerun confirms supported source/host triangles and unchanged unrelated registry exports/hosts. Preserve these useful approach views and the stock-to-anchor distinction in subsequent art work. The close original-rim image is **clearance evidence**, not a resource-overview composition.

**P1-VIS-2 — corrected locally.** At the original x−14.197/z−41.736 failure coordinate, my interpolation of the actual submitted float32 triangle gives rendered height **−21.86995360316621 m**, leaving the recorded eye **0.6399536031662088 m above it**. The full-precision ordinary replay export leaves **0.644378486063097 m** clearance. The new helper refines only the bounded island patch and transition ring; the physical heightfield remains unchanged. My adapted mesh audit reproduces **339,296 samples**, maximum local error **0.025906701 m**. This is a sampled local result, not a continuous/global error bound. Current topology tests find no interior crack/T-junction, preserve remote control cells and check the ramp/deck perimeter.

**P1-VIS-3 — corrected.** Compared with the old alternating deck conflict in 1B `final-workshop-empty-anchor.png`, my independently extracted current deck frames at **40, 42, 44 and 46 s** show stable exposed planking as the viewing direction changes. `terrainSurface.ts` omits only faces covered by the existing opaque deck footprint, with exact boundary cuts. Render topology and physical deck/ramp checks agree. This is sampled motion inspection, not a claim to have watched every video frame.

**Startup-camera exclusions — justified.** I inspected the raw trace neighborhoods as well as rerunning the audit. There is one pose-bearing first route record in each of `trace-final-headland.json` and `trace-final-west-and-controls.json` with the initial menu camera `(25,13,44)` alongside newly populated gameplay HUD data. They occur at entry ticks16682 and9266, frame counters6 and4. The next retained route records use the correct gameplay eye, at frame counters10 and6. Earlier setup logs without player pose are also not gameplay pose evidence. The exclusion is therefore specific to asynchronous entry observation, not a filter hiding sustained underground movement. The remaining **1,524 matched affected-route records** have minimum sampled eye clearance **0.6402778143 m**; all **370** selected-host triangle-ray checks pass. I do not count the two exclusions as same-frame camera agreement.

**Capture jump — reproduced, but not an established product defect.** The author traces contain large view changes immediately after some Return clicks. In my fresh production tab, native T3 click moved to the Return button at approximately `(259,288)`, then delivered a trusted locked `pointermove` of **(−259,−288)** before the lock-change notification. `input.ts` correctly consumed that delta at 0.0025 sensitivity: yaw changed by −0.6475 and pitch by +0.72. A subsequent native **Enter** on the focused Return button captured without any yaw/pitch change. Native inventory I open/close also released/reacquired as intended. This is consistent with automation cursor restoration and supplies the previously missing input explanation; it does not prove an unsolicited human-device jump. No warp-suppression patch is requested on this evidence. A genuine mouse/drag check remains part of later human input validation. Receipt: `browser-capture.json`.

## Costs, limits and follow-up checks

The 1C correction increases the standardized scene roster **391,011→485,460 triangles**, **99→102 meshes**, with **18 materials unchanged**. Terrain itself grows **34,189→80,421 vertices** and **67,640→159,882 triangles**. My rerun confirms aggregate vertex/index buffer growth of **3,451,906 bytes**. The author's one NullEngine creation sample was577→823 ms; my separate single run was approximately689→1018 ms. Neither is a GPU frame-time benchmark. The refinement is bounded and lifetime tests pass; M2 streaming/profile work must include its cost. Do not infer 1080p/60 or a minimum dedicated GPU from this review.

Existing tests and actual retained play establish the scoped behavior, with these limits still open:

- Native lock entry/release is real. Relative movement and selected blur/denial actions in author evidence are synthetic/injected. Native drag tool calls timed out; my bounded trial did not repeat them or claim to resolve them. Native device comfort, OS focus behavior and every browser race are not demonstrated.
- Browser rendering used Linux Chromium headless shell154/SwiftShader with muted audio. Audio event routing/lifecycle passed; listening comfort and mix did not receive a human evaluation.
- Media inspection is named stills and sampled motion/step evidence, not continuous watching of every recording. The rib scenario is explicitly seeded. Emergency/deep-exit fixtures are diagnostics. Ordinary source cycles reuse earned imports.
- The larger menu/notice/air/encounter work and rib **physical collision** redesign remain slice2. End-of-stage Opus review, full fleet/campaign construction, human enjoyment/duration and dedicated-GPU checks remain required later. These are not new blocking findings against the reconciled slice.
